cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: 'Too many connections' (FATAL: sorry, too many clients already) means PostgreSQL hit max_connections and refuses new ones. Troubleshooting means finding who holds connections and what state they are in, using pg_stat_activity.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Count by state, then group by client IP, user and application name. Many active means slow queries or real load; many idle means oversized pools across too many instances; idle in transaction means the app is not closing transactions, which also holds locks. Fix pools, leaks and slow queries; add a pooler.

questions.q: Why not just raise max_connections a lot?
questions.a: Each connection is a separate process with its own memory, and work_mem is per operation, so memory can run out.
The application opened a transaction and is not closing it, which also holds locks.
